meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French Napoleonic tradition with Belgian administrative law and Germanic influences)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Arts. 49-54 freedom of establishment; Art. 63 free movement of capital)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty network (more than 60 BITs in force for Luxembourg)
Luxembourg-China DTA (signed 14 Nov 1994, as amended by Protocol of 7 Nov 2014) and BLEU-China BIT (signed 6 Jun 2005, in force 2009)
Luxembourg-United States DTA (signed 3 Apr 1996, as amended by Protocols of 2004 and 2009)
Luxembourg-Hong Kong DTA (signed 11 Dec 2020, in force 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, including by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 5 January 2023); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE, as amended by the Law of 5 January 2023); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT (as amended); Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector (as amended); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 March 2017 on the risk-based approach
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE is not fully public after the CJEU decision of 22 Nov 2022, Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; access granted to competent authorities, AML supervisors and to private parties demonstrating a legitimate interest in AML/CFT investigations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate shareholder (full corporate chain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs, Cayman CIR, Delaware Secretary of State)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Directors and Shareholders of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate services provider in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the signatory to execute the Luxembourg notarial deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where the state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of each individual UBO, director and manager (with proof of residential address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority or notary public of the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of origin of funds covering the paid-up share capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution holding the blocked capital account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required (original bank certificate issued directly to the notary)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and managers against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, CSSF sanction measures, OFAC SDN/SSI lists and the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) guidance; enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation required for any PEP (Article 3-4, Law of 12 Nov 2004), including family members and close associates of PEPs; screening is repeated throughout the client lifecycle and before every material transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) electronic portal, www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin characters; French is the governing drafting language of the notarial deed and RCS entry; the corporate name of an S.a r.l. must be preceded or followed by the words 'Societe a responsabilite limitee' or the abbreviation 'S.a r.l.'; names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) must be transliterated into Latin characters for the deed and register; the name must not be misleading as to the company's objects or regulated status.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: broker / courtier / securities dealer / valeurs mobilieres
investment fund / fonds d'investissement / SICAV / UCI
professional of the financial sector (PSF) / professionnel du secteur financier
Luxembourg / Luxembourg City / Grand-Duchy (or any term suggesting state patronage or public authority)
European Union / Central Bank / any international public institution
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is valid for 60 days and may not be extended; upon rejection, the applicant may (i) file a new reservation with a modified name, or (ii) request administrative review of the decision by the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days; if the refusal is maintained, appeal lies to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'Arrondissement, Commercial Chamber) within one month of notification; the notary must also verify name admissibility at the signing of the deed and will refuse drafting if the clearance has lapsed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable for the intended license scope. The Law of 10 August 1915 (Article 100-2) requires a real registered office in Luxembourg; the Law of 5 April 1993 and CSSF practice require physical premises, effective administration, AML/CFT compliance officers, staff and systems in Luxembourg for any PSF/MiFID brokerage license. A virtual office is permitted only as an auxiliary correspondence facility and cannot satisfy regulatory substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - quantified probability greater than 75% that an unannounced CSSF on-site inspection (controle sur place) is performed within the first 36 months of operations, given the High_Risk_Special_License classification of retail equities/CFD/derivative brokerage; Article 52 of the Law of 5 April 1993 authorizes the CSSF to inspect without prior notice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability check and reservation at the RCS/Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: name search and reservation are free of charge in the LBR online portal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and certification of foreign corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, incumbency, POAs, passport copies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, UK FCDO, BVI Registry, HK CEDB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille tariffs (approximately USD 20-60 per document) for an estimated bundle of 4-6 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translations of foreign corporate and banking documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermente) recognized in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated sworn translation tariffs; approximately EUR 35 per page for a standard bundle of up to 10 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and AML/KYC UBO file (source of wealth, sanctions/PEP screening, corporate shareholder chain tracing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm / AML compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced due diligence on a High_Risk_Special_License scope under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the blocked capital bank account and bank attestation of payment of share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank practice (account opening fee and attestation fee; approximately EUR 250-350)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Minimum S.a r.l. share capital: EUR 12,000 registered capital with minimum 20% paid-up (EUR 2,400) deposited on a blocked bank account before the notarial deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution holding the blocked account (returned to the company upon registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Articles 710-1 and 710-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended by the Law of 19 August 2016 (not a fee; statutory capital requirement)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized incorporation deed (statuts) and related deed annexes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff under the Law of 8 December 1983; prevailing market EUR 1,500-2,500 per standard S.a r.l. deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the deed in the electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice (RESA fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Obligatory registration in the Register of Commerce and Societies (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No separate registration fee; covered by notarial formalities and the RESA publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration filing in the RBE (Registre des beneficiaires effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: registration in the RBE is free of charge; mandatory filing must be completed within one month of incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office provision - physical office in Luxembourg City (first-year services)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a compliant office lease and substance package for a licensed financial sector company (approximately EUR 2,400 per year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CSSF preliminary regulatory consultation and license-readiness assessment for the PSF/MiFID brokerage scope
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark hourly rates (EUR 350-500 per hour) for CSSF licensing project; Stage 1 retains regulatory read-across only, full license application budgeted at later stage

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 181 to 263 (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on accounting and annual accounts, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of association (acte constitutif) combined with the RCS registration form (déclaration d'inscription) filed electronically by the notary through the LBR/RCS portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A SARL requires minimum subscribed capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash before registration. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account in the name of the company in formation; the bank releases the funds to the company only after RCS registration. Non-cash contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers have adopted the articles of association of [COMPANY] SARL, subscribed in full to [N] shares for an aggregate capital of EUR [●], and that the share capital has been paid up in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [REGISTERED OFFICE], Luxembourg. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed as manager (gérant) with the mandate to represent the Company, and [NAME] is appointed as deputy manager for day-to-day administration. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the managers are authorized to execute the RCS registration, open blocked and operating bank accounts, engage advisors, and file all regulatory applications, including the CSSF financial-sector license, before commencing any brokerage activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of minimum share capital into a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorized by the CSSF (e.g. bank corporate desk) / blocking bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked formation account in the name of the company being formed. Transfer the full subscription amount (minimum EUR 12,000) into the account and obtain a certificate of blockage from the bank. Instruct the bank to block the funds until the RCS registration certificate is produced. The bank's release instruction must be conditional on RCS issuance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the KYC or source of funds, submit the shareholder corporate structure chart and underlying transactional documentation within 5 business days; re-route the deposit to another CSSF-licensed bank if unresolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of incorporation deed before a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (notaire agréé) / Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft articles of association and supporting documents to the notary. The notary verifies capacity, legal object, lawfulness of the activity, share subscription declarations, and manager consents. Sign the notarial deed in person or, where admitted, by proxy with a notarized power of attorney. Obtain the original deed (acte constitutif) and notarial certificates for the filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests modifications, execute a rectification deed or amend the draft and re-notarize; address any concerns about the regulated brokerage purpose by incorporating the CSSF authorization condition into the corporate object.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via www.lbr.lu/eJustice or notary electronic filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the notarized incorporation deed and the RCS registration application electronically. Pay any applicable publication and registration duties. Await the RCS number and the identity verification of managers. Confirm that the registered office is accepted and the legal entity is constituted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS files a rectification query, the notary corrects the fields or submits a supplemental declaration; disputes are cured by filing a request for registration with the Registrar or by judicial rectification before the Luxembourg district court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation extract in the RESA official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations), operated on the LBR portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary or LBR automatically places the mandatory legal publication in RESA. Review the published extract for exact company name, RCS number, corporate object, registered office, and manager names. Save a copy for the corporate record book and CSSF file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains errors, require the LBR to republish a corrected extract and issue a certificate of rectification before any third-party reliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of first board resolution and completion of corporate governance formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders in general meeting / managers (gérants) at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive shareholders' meeting and adopt the first board resolution. Confirm the share subscription table, the registered office, the appointment of managers, the authorized signatories, and the internal delegation restricted to the approved corporate object. Execute the corporate minute book, share register, and RCS update if the registered office must be confirmed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minutes contain a defect, execute a supplementary unanimous shareholders' resolution that ratifies and rectifies the earlier minutes; notify the RCS of any governance changes within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the financial sector license application to the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), 283 Route d'Arlon, L-1150 Luxembourg; online through MyCSSF channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply for the financial sector professional license before commencing any regulated brokerage activity. Assemble the license dossier containing corporate documents, programme of operations, AML/CFT manuals, IT security and business continuity plan, fit-and-proper questionnaires, financial projections and capital attestation. Coordinate the application with the bank account opening and external audit arrangements.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and articles of association
Programme of operations describing brokerage and order routing
AML/CFT policy and internal control manual
Fit and proper questionnaires of managers and qualifying shareholders
Financial projections, solvency plan and capital attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSSF issues an objection or information request, respond within the set deadline; changes to the programme of operations are made and resubmitted. In case of refusal, exhaust the administrative appeal before the Luxembourg administrative courts and apply for a partial license where possible.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to office-based securities brokerage; the relevant licensing authority is the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). The Ministry of the Economy would only intervene for any future physical industrial installation, which is outside the brokerage scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial sector professional license (agrément de professionnel du secteur financier) for the intermediation and execution of transactions in securities and derivative instruments, issued under Article 22-1 of the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement / Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no industrial installation; office-only brokerage activity with no mandatory EIA registration or full environmental impact report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable wastewater, VOC or process-emission thresholds for office activity. For office fit-out, comply with EU Regulation (EU) No 305/2011 on construction products and Luxembourg rules on waste sorting and disposal of electronic equipment via authorized waste streams.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required from the communal fire-prevention consultative commission (commission consultative des édifices communaux) for the registered office; occupational clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workplace safety, ergonomics, first-aid obligations, and safe ESC/strongroom access; CSSF imposes fit-and-proper, physical security, archiving and business-continuity clearance for the brokerage premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes (corporate income tax, net wealth tax, municipal business tax) with portal MyGuichet.lu and e-CDF electronic filing system; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT (TVA) registration and indirect tax compliance with portal Guichet.lu / eTVA (Electronic VAT filing).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate SARL with Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal; the RCS issues a 11-digit registration number (numéro de matricule) which serves as the base corporate tax identification number. Step 2: File the mandatory VAT registration application (Formulaire 640 'Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA') with AEDT after the RCS registration; the AEDT assigns a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro d'identification TVA) prefixed 'LU' plus 8 digits. Step 3: Submit the Luxembourg income tax registration file to the ACD (Bureau d'imposition) of the tax district (Bureau d'imposition SOCARRIS/SARL) for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IF); the ACD issues an assessment file (dossier fiscal) and annual return obligations. Step 4: Register as an employer for PAYE withholding (retenue à la source) if the SARL hires personnel in Luxembourg. Step 5: Confirm registration with the Social Security Centre (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale - CCSS) for social security contributions. The entire registration workflow is coordinated through the independent e-Space on MyGuichet.lu with delegated e-signature capacity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Luxembourg société à responsabilité limitée (SARL) is a resident corporate taxpayer fully subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités - IRC) at 17% including the unemployment fund contribution (contribution au fonds de l'emploi), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal - ICC) at a maximum aggregate rate of approximately 24.94% in Luxembourg City, and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune - IF) at 0.5%; the SARL is fiscally transparent only if expressly elected under the Luxembourg partnership regime, which is unavailable for SARLs, or if organized as a special limited partnership (SCSp); territorial scope: worldwide taxation for Luxembourg-resident SARLs with extensive participation exemption for qualifying shareholdings (≥10% or ≥€1.2 million acquisition price held for 12 months) and no withholding tax on outbound dividends (parent-subsidiary directive) except a 15% domestic rate on non-qualifying distributions; Luxembourg does not maintain a general tax-exempt zone, though the Freeport (Luxembourg Freeport) is a customs bonded warehouse not a corporate tax exemption zone).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not recognize the US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is fixed under the Commercial Law and the Income Tax Law (LIR) based on legal form. However, Luxembourg offers: (1) the partnership look-through election for SARLs is unavailable, but a co-ownership (indivision) or SCSp can be used for transparent vehicles; (2) the group consolidation regime (régime de l'intégration fiscale) effective 2024 allows a 100%-owned Luxembourg parent to consolidate Luxembourg tax results of subsidiaries with a minimum retention period of 5 consecutive fiscal years; (3) the optional payroll withholding election (évaluation forfaitaire) for partly payroll-based benefits; (4) the VAT grouping election (assujettis uniques) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law allows unaffiliated or affiliated taxable persons established in Luxembourg to be treated as a single taxable person for VAT; (5) the hybrid mismatch election must be documented in the tax file (Form 610) to align Luxembourg treatment under ATAD 1/2; (6) the special election for the 80% participation exemption and the 50% gross-wealth exemption for qualifying IP (IP box regime) under Article 50bis LIR. No check-the-box deferral is available for the Luxembourg SARL, which is mandatorily opaque.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA - taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), codified in the amended VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (Loi TVA) implementing the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT). Securities brokerage services provided by a Luxembourg SARL are subject to the B2B place-of-supply rule (Article 48 Loi TVA) with reverse charge for EU clients or outside-scope treatment for third-country clients; domestic retail services to private clients are taxable but exempt without credit (exonération sans droit à déduction) under Article 44 Loi TVA (negotiation/management of securities).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for Luxembourg-established taxable persons engaged in exempt financial activities; the small business franchise regime (régime de la franchise) at Article 57 Loi TVA applies only to an annual taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT), but is explicitly excluded for persons carrying out exempt operations under Articles 43, 44, 148, 149, 150 and 151 Loi TVA (including securities brokerage and other financial services). Therefore a Luxembourg SARL engaged in ISIC 6611 securities brokerage must register for VAT (immatriculation à la TVA) from the first euro of turnover, with no threshold exception. Non-established foreign businesses also have a mandatory zero-euro threshold registration requirement for distance sales and intermediary services. The franchise exclusion applies with EUR 35,000 de minimis for any mixed activity, but the excluded activities kill the franchise.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or pre-clearance digital stamping is in force in Luxembourg for B2B e-invoicing (as of the current compliance cycle). Luxembourg has implemented the EU Directive 2014/55/EU for B2G (business-to-government) e-invoicing; all invoices issued to Luxembourg public-sector bodies (state, municipalities, social security) must be transmitted as structured e-invoices (EN 16931 format, specifically Peppol-BIS 3.0, via the Luxembourg PEPPOL access point). B2B paper/invoice PDFs remain acceptable, but a national mandate for mandatory B2B e-invoicing has been announced by the Luxembourg government (draft budget/conjuncture plans, expected effective fiscal year 2026+): the proposed model is a clearance continuous transaction control (CTC) regime, but the final technical specifications (API, JSON/UBL schema and fiscal stamp) are not yet enacted into the Loi TVA. Until enacted, cross-border B2B transactions with other EU Member States must respect the mandatory e-invoicing rules of the customer's Member State (e.g., France, Italy, Poland, Romania, Belgium, Spain) which creates an indirect e-invoicing obligation. The Luxembourg SARL must therefore: (1) operate a PEPPOL access point or subscribe to a certified service provider for B2G invoicing to Luxembourg public buyers; (2) implement a matrix QR/2D barcode standard on B2C invoices for built-in digital stamping if invoicing in a country where that applies; and (3) archive all invoices (paper or electronic) for 10 years (Article 66 Loi TVA) with a 'séquestre fiscal' filing requirement. Local file archiving must permit AEDT online audit access.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% TVA) applies to: (1) exports of tangible goods transported by the supplier or for the supplier's account to a destination outside the EU, evidenced by the customs export declaration (EX-A) and transport documents, in accordance with Articles 53 and 154 Loi TVA; (2) supplies of services directly and strictly related to the export of goods (transport, handling, freight forwarding, inspection, packaging) under Article 54 Loi TVA; (3) certain services physically performed outside the EU for non-EU business customers, including brokerage of securities on behalf of non-EU counterparties, which under the B2B place-of-supply rule are outside Luxembourg VAT scope entirely; and (4) intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered purchasers (with a valid EU VAT ID in VIES) under Article 51-52 Loi TVA. For a Luxembourg SARL performing offshore securities brokerage (ISIC 6611): equity, CFD and derivative brokerage services to retail clients in third countries are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (B2B rule), or if rendered to private consumers outside the EU, are also outside scope under the business-to-consumer (B2C) place-of-supply rule. It is critical to distinguish zero-rated (0%) from exempt without credit (exonération sans droit à déduction) under Article 44 Loi TVA: securities dealing and negotiation services supplied to Luxembourg private retail clients are exempt without input VAT recovery, not zero-rated. To claim export zero-rating for goods or ancillary services, the SARL must hold (a) the customs export documentation; (b) the transport contract/proof; and (c) the payment evidence. Services linked to exports must be directly traced to a specific export movement; general overhead or back-office services to a broker's own client book do not qualify for zero-rating and remain subject to the exempt/outside-scope analysis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A/DEA) with MRN (Movement Reference Number) accepted by Luxembourg Customs (Administration des douanes et accises)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) / CMR consignment note evidencing cross-border physical shipment
Commercial Invoice (triplicate) matching the export declaration values
Inward Remittance Certificate (from the settlement bank, evidencing hard-currency receipt of the export proceeds on a customer bank account located in Luxembourg)
Brokerage confirmation slip / trade ticket evidencing the offshore securities transaction and the commission structure
Proof of client due diligence (KYC/AML file) confirming non-EU residence for the offshore broker's seat and the beneficial owner's tax residency
VIES confirmation output (EU customer VAT ID validation) for intra-Community zero-rating claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — the Central Bank of Luxembourg, exercising monetary policy, financial stability, balance-of-payments and foreign-exchange administration functions as a member of the Eurosystem; prudential and conduct supervision of the licensed securities brokerage is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) acting as the national competent authority under MiFID II/MiFIR, CRD IV/CRR, and the law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a Eurozone member and maintains full and unrestricted euro convertibility for current-account and capital-account transactions pursuant to Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Neither prior administrative authorisation nor exchange-control licensing exists for inbound equity contributions, outbound profit remittances, dividend distributions, cross-border loan repayments, or commission rebates to foreign introducing brokers. Residual hurdles are purely domestic rules: (i) SARL distribution constraints under the law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Articles 710-1 et seq.), requiring annual-account approval and a positive net-asset test after distribution; (ii) a 15% Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends (0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where an EU/EEA corporate shareholder holds 10% or EUR 1,200,000 for 12 months; reduced or exempt under applicable tax treaties); and (iii) BCL statistical reporting obligations for external financial transactions and CSSF prudential reporting for regulated investment firms. For a CSSF-licensed securities brokerage, client-funds convertibility is additionally constrained by client-asset segregation rules under MiFID II Article 16(8) and CSSF Circular 21/797, which require segregated client money to be held in euro or in other currencies as necessary for settlement, without requiring conversion onshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg and the Eurosystem impose no statutory export-proceeds surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for goods or services, and no analogue exists for cross-border brokerage commissions receivable from non-resident clients. Commission income in foreign currency may remain offshore or be converted freely without BCL approval; the only compliance overlay is the regulatory requirement that client monies be identified, segregated, and reconciled daily, and that a regulated investment firm's own funds be maintained in currency and location consistent with CSSF Circular 21/797 and LCR/NSFR obligations under CRR.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Luxembourg authorises payment institutions, electronic money institutions (EMIs), and specialised Professionals of the Financial Sector (PFS) under the law of 10 August 2015 on payment services and the law of 1 March 2012 on electronic money, all supervised by the CSSF; however, EMIs are not CRR credit institutions and cannot lawfully safeguard retail client money of a MiFID investment firm. The regulated brokerage must segregate client funds at a prudentially supervised credit institution (EEA branch, or a third-country institution under CSSF conditions) pursuant to Article 37-1 of the law of 5 April 1993 and MiFID II Article 16(8). Offshore digital EMIs without an EU/EEA passport or Luxembourg presence are unsuitable for the client-money rail; at most, they may serve as peripheral fee-collection conduits for non-EU clients if they are supervised in a FATF-equivalent jurisdiction and swept daily into the segregated account. The operative model requires account relationships directly with CRR credit institutions; transaction-account EMIs may support operational FX conversion but must be disconnected from the client-money ledger and from any deposit-taking function to avoid unlicensed banking exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is ordinarily required in practice. Luxembourg AML/CFT law (law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02) requires identification and verification of the legal person, its statutory managers, and all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs above 25%) before or during activation of the business relationship. For a High_Risk_Special_License retail securities brokerage, tier-1 Luxembourg banks uniformly require (i) one statutory director or authorised manager and at least one UBO to attend an in-person interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises or before a Luxembourg notary authenticating the powers, and (ii) a second face-to-face compliance interview covering business model, target markets, payment flows, and transaction monitoring. Remote onboarding is legally permissible under inherited CSSF practice using qualified eIDAS signatures, video liveness verification, and independent cross-checks against the RCS and RBE registers; however, a purely remote path is almost never accepted for an offshore-oriented broker in the absence of an established relationship with the same banking group. The account file must include dual-signature bank mandates, board resolutions with notarized specimen signatures, professional indemnity insurance, audited financial statements, and the CSSF licence or formal licence-application proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business profile: retail CFD/equity execution with leverage, high client churn, affiliate-led acquisition, elevated mis-selling and financial-crime risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF licence or formal authorisation application; ESMA product-intervention compliance policy for CFDs (leverage caps, negative balance protection, standardised risk warnings); MiFID II target-market and product-governance assessment; external legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour; audited three-year business plan; client-acquisition channel register with introducing-broker agreements and affiliate oversight procedures; board-approved compliance manual; internal audit charter and complaints-handling procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of beneficial ownership, offshore intermediate shareholding layer, or non-EU UBOs in the ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS excerpt and notarised articles of association; RBE (Luxembourg beneficial-owner register) extract with all natural-person UBOs documented; bank references for UBOs from recognised EU/EEA credit institutions; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files (sale deeds, audited financial statements, tax returns, trust or gift deeds, apostilled and legalised as required); corporate organisation chart traced to ultimate natural persons; negative-media and sanctions screening; PEP assessment at director and UBO level.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment rails: high-velocity Visa/Mastercard card funding for trading accounts with geographically dispersed card-issuing jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS attestation of compliance (SAQ-D or AOC); acquiring and card-brand agreements with registered EU/EEA acquirers; chargeback and refund procedure; 3-D Secure / Strong Customer Authentication implementation; transaction-velocity, AVS/CVV and 3DS-exception fraud-detection policy; daily reconciliation and card-funding clawback mechanism; remote source-of-funds validation using card metadata and digital identity verification for first-card deposits; negative-jurisdiction filter for prohibited card issuers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire concentration: planned material flows to/from non-EU, high-risk, or grey-list jurisdictions linked to underlying trading counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Wire-transfer policy aligned with Regulation (EU) 2015/847 (travel rule) and FATF Recommendation 16; originator/beneficiary information protocol; correspondent banking map with purpose-of-payment taxonomy; real-time sanctions screening and transaction-monitoring architecture; corridor-specific economic-purpose rationale with contractual counterparty due-diligence files; institutional client tiering with enhanced due-diligence algorithm; monetary and volume tolerance thresholds expressly approved by the bank's compliance function.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client-money and liquidity exposure: large segregated client balances, overdraft latency, and risk of commingling between broker wallet engine and segregated account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client-money methodology under CSSF Circular 21/797 (daily reconciliation, own-funds contribution test under Article 37-1 of the law of 5 April 1993); independent client-assets auditor appointment; trustee undertaking and acknowledgment-of-segregation letters; treasury policy with automated cut-off sweeps and cash-concentration structure; intraday and overnight liquidity facility collateralised by eligible securities; quarterly audited client-money reconciliation; distress run-book covering clearing and client-asset return scenarios.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial share capital (SARL statutory floor EUR 12,000, but for a MiFID investment firm holding client assets the CSSF requires initial capital of at least EUR 730,000 under CRD IV Article 28(2)) is wired by SWIFT MT103 from the UBO's bank account to a blocked capital-escrow account opened with a Luxembourg credit institution. The remittance must carry structured payment information referencing the RCS registration number of the company-in-formation, the notarial engagement, and the ECB/BCL balance-of-payments statistical purpose code — typically 'S301 – Equity capital' with the ISO 20022 Category Purpose 'EQUI'. The bank issues an attestation de blocage to the Luxembourg notary, who certifies free disposal before signing the notarised incorporation deed. Post-incorporation shareholder subordinated loans use code 'S302 – Debt instruments' (Category Purpose 'LOAN') and must be documented by written subordination agreements when counted as regulatory capital; CSSF must be informed of any ancillary own-funds instruments. No exchange-control approval is required; the only gates are BCL external-statistics reporting, CSSF capital-adequacy notices, and RCS annual-filing obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA cross-border settlement, including CFD margin calls, equity trades settled via Clearstream or foreign CSDs, and withdrawal payments to non-EEA retail clients, with full originator/beneficiary data under Regulation (EU) 2015/847; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001/pacs.008) for euro transfers inside the EEA, covering dividends to EU shareholders, commission rebates to EU introducing brokers, and payments to Luxembourg tax and social authorities; (iii) SWIFT MT202/MT202COV for correspondent-bank cover payments where the underlying obligation is cleared indirectly, retaining full travel-rule payload; and (iv) irrevocable documentary credits (UCP 600) or documentary collections (URC 522) for ancillary non-brokerage trade flows, which are rarely used in securities brokerage. For regulated securities execution, settlement occurs on a delivery-versus-payment (DVP) basis over TARGET2 securities (T2S) through Clearstream Banking Luxembourg and the relevant CCP; outbound withdrawals to retail clients are paid from the segregated client money account only after payment-out-of-trust verification, AML scoring, and card-scheme fraud checks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward under an ISDA 1992/2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex, hedging EUR/USD, EUR/CHF and EUR/GBP mismatches between foreign-currency client settlements, commission flows and equity clears
FX swap (spot-next and tom-next structures) for intraday and short-tenor liquidity management and temporary reinvestment of foreign-currency client-money surpluses
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) for long-duration hedging of external borrowing or stabilisation of foreign-currency operating income

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) exclusively on non-EEA restricted currencies (e.g., offshore CNY, KRW, INR, BRL) where deliverable forward markets are closed, subject to EMIR clearing and margining thresholds, CRR counterparty credit-risk rules, and the home-jurisdiction FX regulations of the counterparty bank
European-style FX options (vanilla and digital) for asymmetric hedging of contingent settlement exposures, with daily delta monitoring by the treasury function
Collateralised equity return swaps and total-return swaps via prime-brokerage facilities, respecting EU SFTR transparency, MiFID II suitability, and client-appropriateness restrictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) and publication in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the annual accounts within six months after financial year-end; the annual accounts must then be filed with the RCS within one month after approval and in any case no later than seven months after financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file allows the RCS registrar to issue formal notice and may lead to a court order compelling filing under penalty payment (astreinte); administrative and criminal fines up to EUR 1,250 for managers; repeated non-compliance may trigger judicial dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO declaration and confirmation (déclaration et confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (UBO Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least one UBO filing per calendar year; confirmation must be submitted annually on the anniversary of the previous declaration. Any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers exceeding 10%, must be filed within one month after the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per violation for directors and relevant parties; possible court-ordered compulsory filing; persistent non-compliance may lead to administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax annual return (Form 100)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a SARL with a calendar financial year, the return must be filed by 31 December of the following assessment year; electronic filing is required and extensions may be requested.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default tax assessment (taxation d'office); late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on underpaid tax; late-filing penalties up to EUR 2,500 and criminal sanctions for wilful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing is aligned with the corporate income tax return deadline, generally 31 December after the relevant tax year; net wealth tax is assessed annually as of 1 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment, 0.6% monthly late-payment interest, administrative fines up to EUR 2,500, and tax collection enforcement procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CSSF annual AML/CFT compliance report and prudential confirmation for the licensed securities brokerage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end for the annual AML/CFT internal audit and compliance file; prudential and statistical reporting per CSSF circulars applicable to investment firms.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CSSF disciplinary measures; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for legal persons; public warnings, suspension, or revocation of the authorisation for serious or repeated breaches.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Luxembourg SARL, statutory audit is compulsory when more than one of the following three criteria are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 50 employees. A licensed securities brokerage under CSSF supervision is mandatorily audited regardless of size because of its regulated financial-services status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the annual accounts of commercial companies, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; EU-IFRS is applicable to consolidated accounts of EU-listed groups and may be adopted voluntarily by non-listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners, the SARL must file a UBO declaration and confirm it annually. Any share transfer leading to a change in beneficial ownership must be reported within one month; the annual confirmation must reflect the updated shareholding and beneficial-ownership structure as certified by management.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges on Business and Claims
Register of Bearer Shares and Shareholder Loan Certificates where issued

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Aggregate Luxembourg City effective tax rate on resident SARL profits is 24.94% (17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax). No general statutory tax holidays. Available incentives include: 80% IP box exemption (5% effective rate on qualifying IP income), participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, 20% R&D incentives, investment tax credits, and tax consolidation/grouping relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), filed electronically through the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes) via the eCDF/MyGuichet portal. The form consolidates CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a SARL with a 31 December fiscal year-end, Form 500 must be filed no later than 31 December of the following calendar year. For non-calendar-year fiscal periods, the return is due within six months after the fiscal year-end, unless an extension is granted by the tax authorities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, RCS number, tax file number, legal form, registered office and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm Luxembourg registered office and indicate foreign parent entity identifiers. Non-resident managers must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative if the director is unavailable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting reference period, annual accounts currency and consolidation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with CSSF reporting cycle and foreign group consolidation standards; disclose branch or permanent establishment links.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of central administration and strategic decision-making location.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If decisions are taken abroad, document interlocking board minutes and substance to preserve Luxembourg tax residence and treaty access.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit computation: gross receipts, brokerage commissions, CFD/equity dealing gains, fee income, treasury income, and other operating revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include worldwide income because the SARL is resident. Evidence arm's-length charges and document offshore broker revenues separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back and disallowance schedule: non-deductible interest, ATAD restrictions, transfer pricing adjustments, fines, client entertainment, maintenance of shell assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to non-resident related parties must be supported by transfer pricing documentation and beneficial ownership evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carry-forward utilized in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply loss carryforwards within the 17-year statutory limit; substantiate continuity of ownership and business activity in case of foreign shareholder changes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: Luxembourg dividend/capital tax credits, foreign tax credits, deemed withholding tax, R&D and investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign tax credit certificates and Luxembourg withholding vouchers; non-resident parent cannot combine credits within the SARL return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary tax computation: taxable base, progressive CIT 15%/17%, solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For resident SARL, apply full Luxembourg tax base; use the appropriate municipal rate and confirm non-resident source taxation only if treaty article allocates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration, place and date, signature, and professional declaration of correctness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Signature by a Luxembourg-authorized director or admitted fiduciary/tax agent; foreign representatives require a valid power of attorney.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 500 by the deadline triggers ex officio assessment and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax. The statutory late-filing administrative fine ranges from EUR 250 to EUR 12,000. Understatement due to gross negligence can add up to 10–50% of the under-assessed tax; criminal tax fraud leads to higher pecuniary penalties and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive holdings of at least 10% held for 12 months, and further reduced under an applicable double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder claiming treaty relief must be the beneficial owner and submit a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority to the Luxembourg paying agent before the dividend payment. The payer may apply the reduced rate at source. If over-withholding occurs, the recipient files a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes within the statutory limitation period, attaching the TRC, dividend payment evidence and ownership declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg generally imposes no domestic withholding tax on arm's-length cross-border interest or royalties paid by a SARL to non-residents (0%). Interest is recharacterized as a dividend and subject to 15% withholding if paid under excessive debt or profit-participating loan structures; royalties are not subject to source WHT, but treaty and ATAD/transfer pricing rules still apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File required for groups with consolidated turnover equal to or above EUR 50 million; Local File required where annual controlled transactions exceed EUR 100,000; Country-by-Country Report applies at consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply an ESR-like codified statute, but economic substance is enforced through the OECD/BEPS Principal Purpose Test (PPT), the EU General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR), and CSSF sectoral supervision. A securities brokerage SARL must prove real office premises, qualified employees, Luxembourg-based decision-making, independent risk management, operational substance, and adequate accounting records; failure to demonstrate substance results in denial of treaty benefits, loss of participation exemption, and potential management liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting brokerage fee income, running dual off-book client ledgers, fabricating expenses, or filing false annual tax returns to reduce Luxembourg taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex officio reassessment of evaded tax plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; administrative penalty of EUR 250–12,000; criminal tax fraud penalties of up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years; publication of convictions in egregious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors personally orchestrated fraudulent accounting; they become jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties, and are exposed to asset seizures, professional disqualification, travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Luxembourg SARL is a letterbox entity with no employees, premises, or commercial functions; foreign parent controls all decisions and the entity merely channels offshore brokerage commissions to tax-haven recipients while claiming treaty benefits and participation exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty relief under the BEPS MLI Principal Purpose Test; disallowance of participation exemption and loss carryforwards; recharacterization of revenue to the controlling non-resident; additional tax and 50% gross-negligence penalties; possible CSSF de-authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false substance attestations or artificial board minutes are personally liable for restitution of diverted profits, can be stripped of management functions, and may face criminal sanctions including fines, travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing client wire and Visa/Mastercard payments without proper KYC/CDD, failing to report suspicious transactions to the Luxembourg FIU (CRF), commingling segregated client money with corporate funds, or serving sanctioned third parties through the brokerage platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for legal entities; criminal penalties under Luxembourg AML laws of imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 250,000; revocation of financial services authorization and forfeiture of unlawfully held assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable and can be fined, banned from financial-sector management, forced to make full restitution of misappropriated client funds, and imprisoned; courts may freeze personal assets and issue travel bans during criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a retail equities/CFD brokerage in or from Luxembourg without a CSSF license and without a MiFID passport, holding unsegregated client wires, and using card acquiring channels without regulatory approval.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under the Luxembourg law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector: imprisonment of one to five years and fines up to EUR 50,000; CSSF injunctions and administrative fines up to EUR 2,000,000 or 10% of turnover; forced closure and repayment of client funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors knowingly conducted unlicensed financial services for personal gain; they face joint liability for client losses, disgorgement of profits, director disqualification, asset freezing, travel restrictions and imprisonment.
